Those symptoms—tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis—suggest severe respiratory compromise, but a urinary tract infection would not present with these specific findings. I need to know if the distress is worsening over time and whether there is any fever or feeding difficulty.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The clinical presentation of tachypnea, grunting, and retractions, combined with the chest X-ray findings of ground-glass opacity and air bronchograms, is classic for neonatal RDS. Given your age, did your mother have gestational diabetes or were you born premature?
